source.title: Subliminal Steering: Stronger Encoding of Hidden Signals

page_placements.theme: Sensitivity to data-generation and training settings

record.tranche_reason: Tests subliminal transfer with a different teacher-bias intervention: a learned activation-steering vector rather than the original system-prompt conditioning. It also measures hidden-state alignment and vector recovery.
record.gate_note: The study directly tests transfer from filtered numerical outputs. Its plotted comparisons are shown as figures without recoverable numeric values in the text, so those values are recorded as figure only. Detailed per-topic results are present in Figures 6–9 and Table 2 but are not duplicated here. The prompt-based condition is included as a comparison; the study also reports its transfer as noisy and model-dependent.
record.test_reason: The study runs the original prompt-conditioned teacher pipeline as a comparator alongside a new steering-vector teacher. In both, students are fine-tuned on filtered numeric outputs, and the study reports trait transfer (pick rate, P(yc)) against Base and unsteered Control. It also measures hidden-state alignment with the teacher vector and recovers that vector from the data, which bears on D, and varies full vs LoRA fine-tuning, which bears on E. The teacher bias is induced on purpose, as in the original, but transfer to the student is measured as it arises.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Add: the authors argue the low P(yc) understates transfer, and that the limit is whether fine-tuning shifts activations enough to overcome the student's prior and safety tuning, not how well the data encodes the signal. They also concede that some models appear resistant and that results vary across seeds.
record.recipe_differences: Uses filtered, semantically unrelated numerical outputs and student fine-tuning, but implements the teacher bias with a learned activation-steering vector rather than a system prompt. Tests rank-8 LoRA and full fine-tuning.
record.method_sensitivity: Transfer varies by model, bias type and random seed; training method (SGD/LoRA versus Adam/full fine-tuning) is varied. Hidden-state alignment changes with steering window and direction. Vector recovery is reported as sensitive to numerical precision.

fits_no_version.finding: Transfer persists under plain SGD with rank-8 LoRA, given a per-model learning-rate search, contradicting reports that an adaptive optimizer is required.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Robustness to optimizer choice: subliminal transfer does not require adaptive optimizers such as Adam.

record.problems: Most plotted outcomes have no exact values stated in the text. Results vary across topics, seeds and models; the authors acknowledge that some models may be relatively resistant and that hyperparameter failures cannot be ruled out. Complex target probabilities remain low, and generalized misalignment is not measured.
record.rows_left_out: At the 60-row limit, omitted the Base-condition rows from Figure 2, the detailed per-topic pick-rate and probability values in Appendix Figures 6–9, and per-topic recovery values in Table 2. Figure 2's Base condition is not needed to preserve the unsteered-data control comparison; detailed per-topic outcomes were not duplicated.

untested.parts: Code and maths-reasoning outputs; only three-digit number sequences are used.
Entire version; teacher and student always share a base model.
Broad or emergent misalignment and overt harmful generation; only the per-token probability of specific target strings is measured.
Token entanglement, divergence tokens and the gradient argument; only the steering-vector direction is examined, and only under steered teachers.
Other LoRA ranks (only rank 8 is used) and evaluation-prompt variation beyond the fixed evaluation set.
Entire version; no prompt-only insertion of tokens is tested.

missing.what: Peak alignment max s(ℓ) by prompt family (evaluation, number, random prompts) for animal and complex topics. The shift is similar across families, at roughly 0.1–0.3.
Vector recovery fails under prompt-based subliminal learning (preliminary experiments, text only). This limits the steering-direction account to steered teachers.
Vector recovery depends on numerical precision: it converges under fp16 and fails or stalls otherwise. In an ablation, cosine rose monotonically as loss fell.
The Schrodi et al. prompted implementation gives the strongest transfer on Qwen, so prompted-condition results depend on the implementation chosen.

record.verdict_notes: Several points shape how these verdicts should be read. First, the D evidence is partly built in: the teacher bias is a steering vector by design, so finding a steering-like direction in the student and data mainly shows the vector propagates, not that ordinary subliminal learning works this way. Second, the prompted rows (r01–r08) are the closest replication of the original method, and they are mostly negative. Third, the Fig 3 ablations have no unsteered control, only Base. Fourth, the Table 2 text is garbled: per-model complex and animal blocks were reassigned on the basis of value counts (9 animal topics, 8 complex), so per-model complex states are approximate. Finally, the record's C limits_scope label, about targeted rather than broad misalignment, concerns an untested part and was dropped. Figure-only rows report no exact values.

versions.untested_parts: Tests filtered number outputs generated from a steered teacher and a prompt-conditioned comparison. Does not test code or maths outputs.
No teacher–student experiment using different base models is reported.
Tests specific harmful or misleading target statements using their per-token probability, not broad or generalized misalignment.
Tests alignment with and recovery of the steering vector; does not test token entanglement, divergence tokens, or a gradient argument.
Tests plain SGD with rank-8 LoRA and Adam full-parameter fine-tuning. Does not test other LoRA ranks or behavioral evaluation prompts different from training.
No prompt-only insertion of linked tokens without fine-tuning is tested.
